summary: A class describes what data and methods an object has. You create objects from the class with new, and each one keeps its own copy of the data.
notes: Fields like String name; are declared once at the top of the class with their types.
this.name = name; copies the parameter into the field. Without this, both names mean the parameter.
(double) total / scores.size() casts before dividing, so 177 / 2 gives 88.5 instead of 88.
pitfall: Declaring a variable without new, like Student sam; and then calling sam.average(), fails to compile with "variable sam might not have been initialized". Setting it to null instead throws NullPointerException.
